question.text: The equivalent weight of $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3($ Gram molecular weight $=M)$ in the given reaction is $\mathrm{I}_2+2 \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3=2 \mathrm{NaI}+\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_4 \mathrm{O}_6$

solution.text:
Hint: $\mathrm{I}_2+2 \mathrm{Na}_2 \stackrel{+2}{\mathrm{~S}}_2 \mathrm{O}_3=2 \mathrm{NaI}+\mathrm{Na}_2 \stackrel{+2.5}{\mathrm{~S}_4} \mathrm{O}_6$
$n \cdot f=2 \times 0.5=1$
$\therefore$ Number of moles of electron lost per mole of $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3=1$
Hence equivalent weight of $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{1}=\mathrm{M}$
